questions.title: Recursive inference in a scalar linear-Gaussian state model
questions.description: Focused L3 known-theory rederivation evaluation. The target publication identity, theorem statement, proof, reference implementation, and outcomes are withheld from runtime. Let X_0 have distribution N(m_0,P_0), and for t=1,...,T let X_t=X_{t-1}+eta_t and Y_t=X_t+epsilon_t, where P_0, q=Var(eta_t), and r=Var(epsilon_t) are known and strictly positive. The initial state and all process and observation errors are mutually independent, and the errors are iid within their sequences. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX Theory workspace, derive the complete one-step prediction and filtering recursion from conditional Gaussian algebra, not by naming a standard filter. Prove by induction the conditional means and variances, identify the innovation law and likelihood factorization, and justify when standardized innovations are independent N(0,1). Derive the conditional-MSE optimality of each filtered mean and the exact conditional coverage of the requested state interval. Audit indexing, sigma-fields, positivity, initial conditions, and every normalization. Distinguish filtering from smoothing and forecasting, and do not claim unknown-variance estimation, non-Gaussian exactness, nonlinear filtering, asymptotic parameter inference, or independence after data-dependent variance fitting. The required model-authored Python artifact is est_scalar_gaussian_filter and must implement the exact frozen run_estimator(request) contract without calling a prebuilt state-space or filtering routine. Exploratory Python or R may test identities and edge cases. A separately frozen confirmatory evaluator uses fresh linear-Gaussian trajectories, seeds fixed before outcomes, and at least 1500 independent replicates per design. It checks exact executable identity, standardized-innovation calibration and lag behavior, final-state interval coverage with Monte Carlo uncertainty, and paired filtering error against raw observations. These finite experiments test the implementation on the frozen designs only; they do not prove the theory or extend its scope. Source replication, novelty, and Lean formalization are not applicable. Every unresolved mathematical, executable, empirical, or scope gap must remain explicit.

request_fields.name: observations
request_fields.meaning: The ordered scalar observations Y_1 through Y_T.
request_fields.shape: One list of length 1 through 512 containing finite non-Boolean numbers in [-1e6,1e6].
request_fields.indexing: observations[0] is Y_1; no observation corresponds to X_0.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject Boolean, string, null, object, nested, empty, nonfinite, below-domain, or above-domain values rather than coercing, dropping, sorting, clipping, or imputing them.

request_fields.name: initial_mean
request_fields.meaning: The prior mean m_0 of X_0 before observing Y_1.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject nonnumeric, Boolean, nonfinite, or out-of-domain values rather than coercing or clipping them.

request_fields.name: initial_variance
request_fields.meaning: The known strictly positive prior variance P_0 of X_0.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject zero, negative, nonnumeric, Boolean, nonfinite, or out-of-domain values rather than coercing, taking an absolute value, or clipping.

request_fields.name: process_variance
request_fields.meaning: The known strictly positive q=Var(eta_t), common to every state transition.
request_fields.indexing: The first process error moves X_0 to X_1.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject zero, negative, nonnumeric, Boolean, nonfinite, or out-of-domain values rather than coercing, taking an absolute value, or clipping.

request_fields.name: observation_variance
request_fields.meaning: The known strictly positive r=Var(epsilon_t), common to every observation.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject zero, negative, nonnumeric, Boolean, nonfinite, or out-of-domain values rather than coercing, taking an absolute value, or clipping.

request_fields.name: interval_level
request_fields.meaning: The central posterior probability requested for every filtered state interval.
request_fields.indexing: One level shared by all time points.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject values outside the closed domain, strings, Boolean values, null, arrays, objects, or nonfinite values rather than coercing or clipping.

response_fields.name: predicted_means
response_fields.meaning: The conditional means of X_t given Y_1 through Y_{t-1}.
response_fields.indexing: Entry zero predicts X_1 from the prior at time zero.
response_fields.edge_cases: Preserve full floating-point values without rounding.
response_fields.normalization: Use the exact model-implied one-step conditional mean before assimilating observations[t].

response_fields.name: predicted_variances
response_fields.meaning: The conditional variances of X_t given observations strictly before time t.
response_fields.shape: Exactly T finite strictly positive scalars.
response_fields.indexing: Entry zero predicts X_1 from P_0 and the first transition error.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not omit process uncertainty or return standard deviations.
response_fields.normalization: Use variance, not precision or standard deviation.

response_fields.name: innovations
response_fields.meaning: Observation minus its one-step conditional mean.
response_fields.indexing: Entry t uses observations[t] and predicted_means[t].

response_fields.name: innovation_variances
response_fields.meaning: The conditional variances of the innovations.
response_fields.shape: Exactly T finite strictly positive scalars.
response_fields.indexing: Entry t is conditioned on observations strictly before time t.
response_fields.normalization: Include both one-step state prediction uncertainty and observation noise.

response_fields.name: gains
response_fields.meaning: The scalar coefficient multiplying each innovation in the filtered-mean update.
response_fields.shape: Exactly T finite scalars strictly between zero and one.
response_fields.indexing: Entry t updates the prediction at time t.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not return a precision or its complement.

response_fields.name: filtered_means
response_fields.meaning: The conditional means of X_t given Y_1 through Y_t.
response_fields.indexing: Entry t is after assimilating observations[t].
response_fields.edge_cases: Return filtered rather than smoothed or forecast states.
response_fields.normalization: Update the matching one-step prediction with the matching innovation and gain.

response_fields.name: filtered_variances
response_fields.meaning: The conditional variances of X_t given Y_1 through Y_t.
response_fields.shape: Exactly T finite strictly positive scalars.
response_fields.indexing: Entry t is after assimilating observations[t].
response_fields.edge_cases: Return variance, not standard deviation, and preserve positivity.
response_fields.normalization: Use the exact scalar conditional-Gaussian posterior variance.

response_fields.name: standardized_innovations
response_fields.meaning: Each innovation divided by its positive conditional standard deviation.
response_fields.indexing: Entry t uses innovations[t] and innovation_variances[t].
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not center or rescale the sequence using sample estimates.
response_fields.normalization: Use the model-implied conditional variance separately at every time point.

response_fields.name: interval_lower
response_fields.meaning: Lower endpoint of the requested central filtered-state interval.
response_fields.indexing: Entry t uses the filtered distribution at time t.
response_fields.edge_cases: The endpoint must not exceed the matching filtered mean.
response_fields.normalization: Use the standard-normal central quantile implied by interval_level.

response_fields.name: interval_upper
response_fields.meaning: Upper endpoint of the requested central filtered-state interval.
response_fields.indexing: Entry t uses the filtered distribution at time t.
response_fields.edge_cases: The endpoint must not be below the matching filtered mean.
response_fields.normalization: Use the same central standard-normal quantile as interval_lower.

response_fields.name: log_likelihood
response_fields.meaning: The joint log density of Y_1 through Y_T under the supplied known model.
response_fields.edge_cases: Include every Gaussian normalizing constant and use natural logarithms.
response_fields.normalization: Sum the exact one-step Gaussian innovation log densities.

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly the six declared fields and the response exactly the eleven declared fields. Missing, extra, malformed, coercible-only, nonfinite, or out-of-domain values are rejected.
Every response sequence is generated by the exact one-step prediction and conditional-Gaussian filtering recursion for the declared random-walk state model, with process noise entering before Y_t.
Entry t may use observations only through time t; later observations never alter an earlier filtered entry.

Adding the same finite constant to initial_mean and every observation adds it to predicted means, filtered means, and interval endpoints while leaving innovations, variances, gains, standardized innovations, and log_likelihood unchanged.

Multiplying observations and initial_mean by positive b and all three variances by b^2 scales means, innovations, and intervals by b, scales variances by b^2, preserves gains and standardized innovations, and shifts log_likelihood by -T log(b).
Repeated calls with the same request return the same JSON value and do not mutate the request, use random state, read files, invoke subprocesses, or use the network.

empirical_claims.meaning: For every frozen valid request, the candidate is compared with an independent exact scalar conditional-Gaussian implementation across every response sequence and invariant.

Across fresh trajectories from each frozen declared model, standardized innovations are assessed for zero mean, unit second moment, and negligible lag-one correlation using predeclared Monte Carlo uncertainty bounds.
Across independent fresh trajectories, the final filtered interval's state coverage is compared with interval_level using a predeclared Monte Carlo standard-error bound.
Across each frozen model, squared filtered-state error is paired with squared raw-observation error and must show positive mean improvement by a predeclared standard-error margin.
State-model designs, lengths, seeds, at least 1500 independent replicates per design, estimator requests, summaries, and acceptance bounds are evaluator-owned and frozen before the product run.

The experiment assesses one implementation under finitely many scalar linear-Gaussian known-variance designs only. It is not proof and does not validate smoothing, parameter estimation, nonlinear or non-Gaussian filtering, missing observations, or asymptotic inference.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: For every valid bounded request, run_estimator performs one chronological finite pass and returns exactly one response without optimization, randomization, file access, network access, subprocesses, or request mutation.
